lessons.title: What is gamelan?
lessons.summary_nl: Wat is gamelan? Het woord, de balungan als 'skelet'-melodie, leren op het gehoor en de omgangsvormen rond de instrumenten.
lessons.summary_en: Gamelan explained from scratch: what the word means, the balungan as the 'skeleton' melody, learning by ear, and the etiquette of the gamelan.
lessons.oefening_nl: Luister naar een opname en probeer de gong te horen.

key_ideas: Gamelan comes from gamel, a kind of hammer: the instruments are struck, with mallets called tabuh.
Karawitan is the wider word: gamelan music as a whole, singing included.
Usually only the balungan, the 'skeleton' melody, is written down. Notation is a reminder; the sound comes first.
Etiquette: shoes off, sit on the floor, and never step over an instrument. Say 'nuwun sewu' when you pass.
sheet.practice: Listen to a recording of Central Javanese gamelan. Find the big gong and feel the cycle come round.

quiz.question: Where does the word gamelan come from?
quiz.explanation: Gamel is a hammer: the instruments are struck.

quiz.question: What is usually written down in gamelan notation?
quiz.explanation: The other parts are learned by ear, from patterns.

quiz.question: What should you never do near a gamelan?
quiz.explanation: Walk around it, bend low and say nuwun sewu.

quiz.question: What does the course say about mistakes?
options: Be aware of them, but keep trying things out
Stop playing when you make one
quiz.explanation: Learning should be relaxed.

lessons.title: The instruments and their roles
lessons.summary_nl: Een rondgang langs alle instrumenten: gongs, kenong en kempul, sarons, slenthem, bonang, de zachte instrumenten, de stemmen en de kendhang.
lessons.summary_en: A tour of the ensemble: the gongs that mark the structure, the sarons and slenthem that play the balungan, the bonang, the soft instruments, the voices and the drum.
lessons.oefening_nl: Noem bij een foto van een gamelan de instrumenten bij naam.

key_ideas: A full gamelan has 40 to 60 instruments, often a double set: one sléndro, one pélog.
Three roles: gongs mark the structure, the drum controls time, the melodic instruments carry the melody in layers.
Gong ageng, kempul, kenong, kethuk and kempyang are the 'punctuation' of the music.
Balungan instruments from low to high: slenthem, demung, saron barung, saron panerus (peking).

words.meaning: largest gong, ends the longest cycle
the music from gong to gong
large kettle gongs, divide the gongan

sheet.practice: Look at a photo of a gamelan and name every instrument you can.

quiz.question: Which instrument marks the end of the longest cycle?
quiz.explanation: The music between two gong strokes is a gongan.

quiz.question: Who leads the tempo in gamelan?
quiz.explanation: There is no conductor; the kendhang leads time, the rebab leads the melodic flow.

quiz.question: Which saron is the smallest and highest?
quiz.explanation: The saron panerus is also called peking.

quiz.question: What do the kenong do?
options: Divide each gongan into equal phrases
quiz.explanation: After the gong, the kenong is the most important structural instrument.

lessons.title: Tuning and notation
lessons.summary_nl: Sléndro en pélog, pathet, de cijfernotatie (Kepatihan), de gatra, de structuursymbolen en balungan mlaku en nibani.
lessons.summary_en: Sléndro and pélog, the idea of pathet, Kepatihan cipher notation, the gatra, the structure symbols, and balungan mlaku and nibani.
lessons.oefening_nl: Lees een gatra hardop: ji, ro, lu, ma, nem.

key_ideas: Laras means tuning system. There are two: sléndro (5 tones) and pélog (7 tones).
There is no standard tuning: every gamelan has its own.
Kepatihan cipher notation: numbers are tones, dots above/below mark high/low register, a dot alone is a rest.
Four beats make a gatra. The weight falls at the end: count towards four.

words.word: ji, ro, lu, pat, ma, nem, pi

words.meaning: balungan with a tone on every beat
balungan with a rest between tones

sheet.practice: Say the sléndro names out loud while you look at the numbers: ji, ro, lu, ma, nem.

quiz.question: Which number is missing in sléndro?
quiz.explanation: Sléndro uses 1 2 3 5 6.

quiz.question: What does a dot in place of a number mean?
options: A rest: the previous tone keeps ringing
quiz.explanation: A dot above or below a number changes the register; a dot alone is a rest.

quiz.question: Where does the weight fall in a gatra?
quiz.explanation: The gong also falls on the last beat.

quiz.question: What is the Javanese name for tone 5?
quiz.explanation: Ji, ro, lu, pat, ma, nem, pi.

lessons.title: Your first piece
lessons.summary_nl: Zitten en dempen, een oefening op vijf tonen, de lancaran-vorm en een oefengongan om mee te spelen, langzaam en iets sneller.
lessons.summary_en: Sitting and damping, a five-tone drill, the lancaran form, and a practice gongan to play along with, slow and medium.
lessons.oefening_nl: Speel de oefengongan mee op saron, of tik hem op tafel.

key_ideas: Sit cross-legged, back straight, mallet in the right hand.
Damping: the left hand stops the previous key at the moment the right hand strikes the next one.
A lancaran has 16 beats: four gatra in one gongan.
Kethuk on beats 1 and 3, kempul on beat 2 (not in the first gatra), kenong on beat 4, gong on beat 16.

words.meaning: a phrase closed by the kenong

sheet.practice: Play the practice gongan (.3.2 .5.3 .6.5 .3.2) slowly on a saron, or tap it on a table and sing the names.

quiz.question: Which hand damps on the saron?
quiz.explanation: The left hand grasps the key you just played.

quiz.question: How many beats does a lancaran gongan have?
quiz.explanation: Four gatra of four beats.

quiz.question: In a lancaran, where does the kenong play?
quiz.explanation: The gong sounds together with the last kenong.

quiz.question: What matters more when you start?
quiz.explanation: Slowly is fine.

lessons.title: Irama: time that breathes
lessons.summary_nl: Wat irama is, de vijf niveaus, één gatra in drie irama, en de trommelaar die elke overgang leidt.
lessons.summary_en: What irama is, the five irama levels, one gatra heard in three irama, and the drummer who leads every change.
lessons.oefening_nl: Tel bij een opname de peking-slagen per balungan-tel: twee, vier of acht?

key_ideas: Irama is about tempo and density: how many notes the elaborating instruments play per balungan beat.
Count the peking: lancar 1, tanggung 2, dadi 4, wilet 8, rangkep 16.
The balungan melody stays the same; only the space around it changes.
The kendhang leads every change of tempo and irama.

words.meaning: the relation of tempo and density

sheet.practice: With a recording: find the balungan beat and count the peking notes against it. Two, four or eight?

quiz.question: In irama dadi, how many peking notes per balungan beat?
quiz.explanation: Tanggung 2, dadi 4, wilet 8.

quiz.question: Who decides the irama?
quiz.explanation: The kendhang leads the ensemble.

quiz.question: When the irama gets slower, what happens to the balungan melody?
options: It stays the same, only wider
quiz.explanation: Only the space around it changes.

quiz.question: Where is irama lancar used?
quiz.explanation: You played it in lesson 4.

lessons.title: The peking and interlocking
lessons.summary_nl: De peking: nacah lamba en nacah rangkep, Solo- en Yogya-stijl, in elkaar grijpend spel (pinjalan, imbal) en een oefenloop.
lessons.summary_en: Nacah lamba and nacah rangkep on the peking, Solo and Yogya style, pinjalan and imbal, and a practice loop to play along with.
lessons.oefening_nl: Speel de peking-oefenloop mee: elke toon twee keer.

key_ideas: The peking is the smallest saron; its style is called nacah, 'chopping'.
Nacah lamba: every balungan note twice. Nacah rangkep: four notes per beat, taking the notes in pairs.
Solo style follows the beat; Yogya style anticipates it. This course follows Solo style.
Interlocking: pinjalan (demung and slenthem) and imbal (two instruments of the same kind).
sheet.practice: Play the practice loop on the peking: every note twice, Solo style.

quiz.question: In nacah lamba, the peking plays each balungan note...
Which style does this course follow?
quiz.explanation: In Solo style the pair starts with the balungan note.

quiz.question: What is pinjalan?
quiz.explanation: The slenthem plays the same notes half a beat later.

quiz.question: What is the peking mallet made of?
quiz.explanation: A mallet made of horn.

lessons.title: The bonang
lessons.summary_nl: De bonang barung en panerus en drie technieken: gembyangan, mipil en imbal, plus de sekaran.
lessons.summary_en: The bonang barung and panerus, and three techniques: gembyangan, mipil and imbal, with sekaran at the end of a phrase.
lessons.oefening_nl: Zing het mipil-patroon: ro lu ro, ro ji ro.

key_ideas: Bonang barung and bonang panerus (an octave higher); played with two padded sticks.
The bonang anticipates the melody and so guides the sarons.
Gembyangan: two kettles an octave apart. Mipil: single tones in pairs. Imbal: barung and panerus interlock.
A sekaran ('flowering') is an ornament that leads into the goal tone.
sheet.practice: Sing the mipil pattern: ro lu ro, ro lu ro, ro ji ro, ro ji ro. Then tap it on two cups.

quiz.question: Why must a bonang player know the piece well?
options: Because it plays the gong part
Because the bonang anticipates and guides the sarons
quiz.explanation: It plays ahead of the balungan.

quiz.question: What is gembyangan?
options: Two kettles an octave apart at the same time
quiz.explanation: Used on the off-beats in a lancaran.

quiz.question: What does mipil mean?
options: To pick off one by one
quiz.explanation: Single tones, in pairs.

quiz.question: In imbal, does the bonang still lead the sarons?
options: No, it creates a lively background
quiz.explanation: Imbal is for exciting sections.

lessons.title: Ladrang Wilujeng
lessons.summary_nl: De vormen ketawang en ladrang, en de ngelik van Ladrang Wilujeng (sléndro manyura) om mee te spelen.
lessons.summary_en: The ketawang and ladrang forms, one ladrang cycle, and the ngelik of Ladrang Wilujeng (sléndro manyura) to play along with.
lessons.oefening_nl: Speel Ladrang Wilujeng mee, eerst langzaam, dan met peking.

key_ideas: In ketawang and ladrang the kethuk and kempyang play a gentle pattern in every gatra.
Ketawang: two kenongan of 8 beats (16 in total). Ladrang: four kenongan (32 beats).
In a ladrang the kempul plays in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th kenongan, not in the 1st.
Ladrang Wilujeng (sléndro manyura): wilujeng means safety, well-being. We played its ngelik.
sheet.practice: Play the ngelik of Ladrang Wilujeng slowly on a saron; then again with the peking.

quiz.question: How many beats does a ladrang gongan have?
quiz.explanation: Four kenongan of eight beats.

quiz.question: In which kenongan of a ladrang does the kempul NOT play?
quiz.explanation: It plays in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th.

quiz.question: What does wilujeng mean?
quiz.explanation: One of the best-known pieces.

quiz.question: In Ladrang Wilujeng, where does the gong fall?
quiz.explanation: A dot below the six means low six.

lessons.title: The kendhang
lessons.summary_nl: De vier soorten kendhang, de vijf basisslagen (dhah, thung, ket, tong, tak) en hoe de trommelaar tempo en irama leidt.
lessons.summary_en: The four kinds of kendhang, the five basic drum strokes (dhah, thung, ket, tong, tak), and how the drummer leads tempo and irama.
lessons.oefening_nl: Zeg de vijf lettergrepen hardop en tik ze op tafel.

key_ideas: The kendhang is a two-headed drum, played with bare hands.
Four kinds: kendhang ageng, ketipung, wayangan and ciblon. Ageng + ketipung together = kendhang kalih.
Five basic strokes: dhah, thung, ket, tong, tak.
The drummer sets the irama, leads the tempo and signals the end.

words.meaning: open stroke, edge of the large head
open stroke, middle of the large head
closed slap on the small head

sheet.practice: Say the five syllables out loud with the drum, then tap them: right hand for the first three, left hand for the last two.

quiz.question: Which drums together form kendhang kalih?
quiz.explanation: Kalih means two.

quiz.question: Which stroke is a closed slap on the small head?
quiz.explanation: Tak uses the fingers and part of the palm.

quiz.question: Does the drum have to match the gamelan's tuning?
quiz.explanation: It is tuned to suit the drum and the style.

quiz.question: Which drum has lively patterns from the dance?
quiz.explanation: The kendhang ciblon.

lessons.title: Pathet
lessons.summary_nl: De zes pathet, drie frases die op hun sterke toon eindigen, de volgorde door de nacht en pathet in de gongpartij.
lessons.summary_en: The six pathet of sléndro and pélog, three phrases that come to rest on their strong tone, the order of pathet through the night, and pathet in the gong part.
lessons.oefening_nl: Zoek bij een stuk de toon waarop de gong valt: twee, vijf of zes?

key_ideas: Pathet literally means 'to restrain': some tones matter more, the melody stays in a range.
Sléndro: nem, sanga, manyura. Pélog: lima, nem, barang.
A first clue: the tone where the gong falls (often 2 in nem, 5 in sanga, 6 in manyura).
In a wayang night: nem before midnight, sanga in the middle of the night, manyura towards dawn.
sheet.practice: Listen to a piece and find the tone where the gong falls. Two, five or six? That is your first guess at the pathet.

quiz.question: What does pathet literally mean?
quiz.explanation: It organises the tones.

quiz.question: Which sléndro pathet closes the night, towards dawn?
quiz.explanation: Manyura has the highest range.

quiz.question: A sléndro phrase ends on low 5. Which pathet is a good first guess?
quiz.explanation: In sanga, 5 and 1 stand out.

quiz.question: How many pathet are there in total?
quiz.explanation: Three in sléndro and three in pélog.

lessons.title: Soft instruments and voices
lessons.summary_nl: De drie groepen van Sumarsam en de 'inner melody', rebab, gendèr, gambang, siter en suling, pesindhen en gérong, en luid tegenover zacht spelen.
lessons.summary_en: Sumarsam's three groups of instruments and the inner melody, the rebab, gendèr, gambang, siter and suling, the pesindhen and gérong, and loud versus soft playing.
lessons.oefening_nl: Probeer bij zacht spel elke stem apart te horen.

key_ideas: Sumarsam's three groups: melody (elaborate, balungan, in between), time (kendhang), structure (gongs).
No instrument plays 'the' melody; each expresses a shared inner melody in its own way.
Rebab: melodic leader in soft playing. Gendèr: two mallets, damping. Gambang: wooden, octaves. Suling: free rhythm.
Voices: pesindhen (female soloist, free across the beat) and gérong (male chorus, in tempo).
sheet.practice: Listen to soft playing and try to pick out each voice: rebab, gendèr, gambang, suling, pesindhen.

quiz.question: Which instrument is the melodic leader in soft playing?
quiz.explanation: It often plays the introduction.

quiz.question: How does the pesindhen sing?
options: Ornamented, floating freely across the beat
quiz.explanation: The gérong sings in fixed tempo.

quiz.question: What is the gambang made of?
quiz.explanation: A wooden xylophone, mostly in octaves.

quiz.question: In loud playing, which instruments lead?
quiz.explanation: The soft instruments are silent.

lessons.title: From buka to suwuk
lessons.summary_nl: Hoe een stuk begint (buka, senggrengan), de delen (ompak, ngelik), het einde (suwuk) en srepegan om mee te spelen.
lessons.summary_en: How a piece begins (buka, senggrengan), its sections (ompak, ngelik), how it ends (suwuk), and the srepegan form to play along with.
lessons.oefening_nl: Speel de srepegan mee op saron of kenong.

key_ideas: Buka: one instrument plays the introduction; the ensemble joins on the gong.
Senggrengan: a short rebab melody before a soft piece, showing tuning and pathet.
Ompak (repeated first section) and ngelik (higher section). Suwuk: the ending.
Srepegan (wayang): kenong on every beat, kempul on every second kenong, kethuk between the beats.
sheet.practice: Play the srepegan on a saron, or play the kenong part: one stroke on every note.

quiz.question: What is the buka?
quiz.explanation: Usually rebab or bonang; the ensemble joins on the gong.

quiz.question: In srepegan, how often does the kenong play?
quiz.explanation: That gives srepegan its tension.

quiz.question: What is the suwuk?
quiz.explanation: The drummer slows down, the gong closes.

quiz.question: Who decides when srepegan moves on in a real performance?
quiz.explanation: The number of notes is not fixed.

lessons.title: Pélog
lessons.summary_nl: De zeven tonen van pélog en de drie vijftoonsladders, de pélog-pathet, de pélog-bonang en de gedeelde toon (tumbuk).
lessons.summary_en: Pélog's seven tones and three five-tone scales, the pélog pathet, the pélog bonang, and the shared tone (tumbuk) between sléndro and pélog.
lessons.oefening_nl: Speel de zeven tonen langzaam op en neer, en demp elke toon.

key_ideas: Pélog has seven tones with clearly unequal steps.
Sumarsam: pélog is built from three five-tone scales (1 2 3 5 6 / 1 2 4 5 6 / 2 3 5 6 7).
Pélog pathet: lima, nem, barang. Barang uses 7 and avoids 1.
Sléndro and pélog sets usually share one tone, the tumbuk (6 or 5).

words.meaning: shared tone of the sléndro and pélog sets

sheet.practice: If you can reach a pélog saron, play the seven tones slowly up and down, damping each one.

quiz.question: How many tones does pélog have per octave?
quiz.explanation: One to seven.

quiz.question: Which pélog pathet uses tone 7 and avoids tone 1?
quiz.explanation: On the pélog bonang, 7 takes the place of 1.

quiz.question: What is the tumbuk?
options: The tone shared by the sléndro and pélog sets
quiz.explanation: Usually tone 6 or 5.

quiz.question: Which five tones make the third pélog scale?
quiz.explanation: It uses 7 instead of 1.

lessons.title: The bubaran
lessons.summary_nl: De bubaran-vorm, balungan mlaku, en een bubaran in pélog om naar te luisteren en mee te spelen.
lessons.summary_en: The bubaran form, balungan mlaku, and a bubaran in pélog to listen to and play along with.
lessons.oefening_nl: Speel de bubaran mee, en probeer hem ook in sléndro.

key_ideas: Bubar means to break up: a bubaran is often played as guests leave.
Same gong structure as the lancaran: 16 beats, four kenongan.
But: balungan mlaku (a note on every beat), in irama tanggung or dadi.
Example (Drummond): 6532 6532 .323 6532.
sheet.practice: Play the bubaran on a saron. It only uses 2 3 5 6, so try it in sléndro too and hear the difference.

quiz.question: When is a bubaran often played?
options: At the end of an event
quiz.explanation: Bubar: to disperse.

quiz.question: How does a bubaran differ from the lancaran in lesson 4?
quiz.explanation: The gong structure is the same.

quiz.question: How many beats in a bubaran gongan?
quiz.explanation: Four kenongan of four beats.

quiz.question: Why can you also play this bubaran in sléndro?
options: Pélog and sléndro are the same
quiz.explanation: Those tones exist in both tunings.

lessons.title: First steps on the gendèr
lessons.summary_nl: Hoe gendèr-spelers leren, de slagstokken vasthouden, twee manieren van dempen en vier oefeningen van Sumarsam.
lessons.summary_en: How gendèr players learn, holding the mallets, two damping techniques, and four exercises from Sumarsam for right hand, left hand and both hands.
lessons.oefening_nl: Doe de vier oefeningen langzaam, elke dag een paar minuten.

key_ideas: Gendèr is learned pattern by pattern (cèngkok), but listening and ensemble playing make the player.
Right hand: loose fist, palm down. Left hand: palm faces right, thumb around the end of the handle.
Damping 1: damp just after the next stroke (smooth). Damping 2: damp at the exact moment (only when fast).
Four exercises: right hand, left hand, both together (gembyangan), and alternating.
sheet.practice: Do the four exercises slowly, a few minutes every day.

quiz.question: What makes a good gendèr player, according to Sumarsam?
options: Listening a lot and playing in the ensemble
quiz.explanation: The patterns help, but listening comes first.

quiz.question: In the first kind of damping, when do you damp?
quiz.explanation: So the tones join smoothly.

quiz.question: When do you use the second kind of damping?
options: Only when the playing is too fast
quiz.explanation: Damp at the exact moment.

quiz.question: Which pieces does Sumarsam suggest to start on the gendèr?
quiz.explanation: Their patterns repeat.

lessons.title: Gendhing, and how to keep learning
lessons.summary_nl: De grote vorm gendhing (mérong, ompak, inggah), kethuk 2 kerep, gamelan in het Javaanse leven, hoe je verder leert, en een terugblik.
lessons.summary_en: The large gendhing form (mérong, ompak, inggah), kethuk 2 kerep, gamelan in Javanese life, and how to keep learning, with a look back at all sixteen lessons.
lessons.oefening_nl: Zoek een groep en speel samen.

key_ideas: Gendhing: both the word for a composition and a large form with mérong and inggah.
Mérong: calm, irama dadi. Ompak: short transition, signalled by the drummer. Inggah: melody often from the mérong.
Kethuk 2 kerep: 16-beat kenongan, 64 beats per gongan. Kethuk arang: kethuk every 16 beats.
Keep learning: listen, play in a group, try every instrument, sing the balungan, ask experienced players.
sheet.practice: Find a group near you and play together.

quiz.question: What are the two main sections of a gendhing?
quiz.explanation: With an ompak between them.

quiz.question: How many beats in a gongan of a mérong kethuk 2 kerep?
quiz.explanation: Four kenongan of 16 beats.

quiz.question: Who signals the transition (ompak) to the inggah?
quiz.explanation: With a change of tempo and irama.

quiz.question: Where is gamelan mainly heard in Java?
quiz.explanation: It is enjoyed as part of the occasion.
